bounds.proof:
# Checked broad-phase bounds extraction

This isolated candidate starts at own commit `fc88da4205dd62f7f4ea33cab624fc51e55cd108`. Its only production edit is `source/packages/physics2d/kernel/src/world.rs`; its new private regression module is `world_bounds_tests.rs`. The immutable `control` tree and full initial file hashes are retained in `source-manifest.json`. No live file, public API, scene, tolerance, solver arithmetic, pin or retained manifold reference changes.

## Validation lifetime and private call domain

`World::step` is the sole caller of private `World::broad_phase`. The existing complete current-data preflight checks body poses and current shape cores, as well as graph ownership: every current shape is listed exactly once by an in-range body and `shape.body` agrees with that owner. It refuses malformed counts, nonfinite used vertices/normals/radii/poses, negative radii, stale owners, orphan shapes and duplicate ownership before broad-phase refits.

After that completed preflight and before the refits, the only operations are the existing `dt` decision, `Counts` reset and checked frame-number increment. None changes a core or pose. Each core and pose is an ordinary value/array owned by `World`; the exclusive `&mut World` call has no user callback or intervening mutation opportunity. Broad-proxy placement changes broad storage, not cores or body poses. This is a certificate for the same call stack and current values, with no cross-frame cache.

The new private `bounds_from_validated` is called only by that refit path and by checked public `bounds_of`. Public `bounds_of` keeps `validate_collision_core(core)?` before `validate_collision_pose(xf)?`, then delegates. Shape creation still calls checked `bounds_of`. The helper source copies the original first-vertex transform, remaining-vertex transforms, component min/max reductions, radius expansion and final four-coordinate finiteness refusal verbatim. It retains the original `ArithmeticOverflow` outcome for a finite core/pose whose derived box overflows. No rollback guarantee is added; errors arising after preflight retain the existing partial-step behavior.

## Exactness and error coverage

The three new tests compare the helper and public route against the verbatim original checked implementation, including exact `to_bits()` on every successful coordinate and exact error variants:

- 960 validated-input cases: counts 1 through 8; positive/negative zero, the minimum positive subnormal, ordinary and maximum finite radii; signed-zero, ordinary, maximum finite and subnormal vertices; six finite transforms, including nonunit/zero rotations permitted by the public bounds function and overflow-producing finite values. Unused vertex slots contain NaN/infinity and remain unused.
- Eight malformed used-input mutations compare public error and `World::step` preflight refusal. The core-before-pose error priority and unchanged frame number on preflight refusal are explicit.
- A finite-input derived-overflow world passes the existing shape/body/pose preflight helpers and is refused by public bounds, the private helper and `World::step` with `ArithmeticOverflow`.

The complete native package run passes 75 units (72 unchanged existing units, including per-visit scalar/SIMD shadows, plus these three), all existing integration/input/domain/exact-manifold/pinned-scene tests and both doctests. The strict physical collector passes 29/29 bars without missing or duplicate cases: 28 legacy bars plus the required 1:1000 contact stack. CCD remains separate T-11/127.y work. Both the immutable control and candidate shipped `simd128` Wasm check modules pass all three checks, preserving hashes `9ffefc83c3a99be4`, `95a47530df180011`, `92db6847c4e919d4`. No re-pin is accepted.

## Compiled work, not a timing estimate

`compiled-work.mjs` reads actual release LLVM/native output and the shipped stripped `simd128` Wasm, without optimizer passes or rewriting. Full inventories and extracted observed callees/callers are retained under `compiled/`; `compiled-work.json` records artifact hashes and operation counts.

The emitted native broad-phase function still has the same 2,030 LLVM lines, 10 floating comparisons and 239 branches. Its refit call changes from checked `bounds_of` to `bounds_from_validated`. The checked public wrapper remains emitted and calls the private helper after validation. In the refit's callee, branch-inclusive static LLVM counts change as follows:

| Emitted refit callee | `llvm.fabs` calls | `fcmp` operations | `br` operations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original checked `bounds_of` | 37 | 38 | 42 |
| Private derived-only helper | 1 | 1 | 12 |

These are static counts across all unrolled count/error branches, not per-quad dynamic instruction counts. The remaining vector absolute-value/comparison is the final derived-box finiteness check. Compiler vectorization of native bounds math also changes, so no claim is made that the entire native callee differs only by removed validation instructions.

In the shipped Wasm, the broad-phase refit caller is observed function `$83`; it calls original checked bounds `$17` in the control and derived-only helper `$75` in the candidate. These identities are checked by the inventory script against the retained disassembly. Both observed bounds callees retain exactly 26 `f32.add`, 32 `f32.mul` and 10 `f32.sub` static operations across the unrolled vertex paths. Original scalar finite-check lowering contributes 35 `i32.shl`, 17 `i32.lt_u`, 18 `i32.le_u` and two vector finite predicates; the derived-only callee has zero of those scalar operations and one vector finite predicate. The original radius-negative check accounts for `f32.lt` 15 versus 14. Final derived-coordinate refusal and all physical min/max comparison work remain.

At source level, one valid quad refit avoids 17 core scalar finite predicates (radius plus eight vertex and eight normal coordinates), four pose scalar finite predicates, and the duplicate core-domain decisions. This is a source work count, not 21 machine instructions: pose and final-box predicates can be vectorized, and Rust array-bound safety checks remain. Public callers retain every original check. Module-wide opcode differences are not the claim because valid public/creation paths remain checked and compiler outlining changes layout.

The immutable control artifact is `bounds-control.wasm`, SHA256 `0550ea88dd7753ae6c23e7e5a6010c5c3d79c9dcaf4f2311a3320b7c013e498b` (268,133 bytes). The isolated candidate is `bounds-candidate.wasm`, SHA256 `41198d8995299178be342e4f8e68ef870abb5822c30685f40a4b4e9859f88ddd` (266,992 bytes). File sizes include metadata and do not establish a runtime speed gain. No benchmark was run for this item.

All build/test commands and their hard deadlines are retained in `native-job.json` and `validation-jobs.json`; successful bounded logs and the strict collector result are named and hashed in `evidence.json`. Root owns combination, fresh matched measurement and full landing gates.

tests.source: Full final source native suite; all existing scalar/SIMD scene hashes, per-visit shadows, lifecycle/resource and integration tests pass. Existing opt-in timing tests remain unchanged.

dynamicWork.limitations: Test hooks can inhibit optimizer removal; separate uninstrumented native release control-flow proof establishes production bypass. Counts are predicate evaluations, not machine instructions or a speed claim.

planner.proof:
# Lazy eligibility for rejected support components

Isolated own baseline: `fc88da4205dd62f7f4ea33cab624fc51e55cd108`. Release source changes exactly three existing component eligibility conjunctions from eager `valid &= predicate` to lazy `valid = valid && predicate`. No topology, layout, settings, physical expressions, scene, pass count, predicate or pin changes. Test-only hooks and the immutable eager reference are excluded from release builds.

`valid` starts true for each DFS seed and only accumulates conjunctions until that component ends. Once false, no later eligibility result can restore it. Degree, joint membership and `fixed_domain` are pure reads on the actual validated frame: the last checks current restitution and immutable original approach, returns bool, writes nothing and emits no Result. Skipping those reads after false preserves final validity. Accepted components execute all predicates in their original order. Rejected components still take the same continue before path construction.

Every seed, stack pop, member push, adjacency-edge traversal, visited mark and terminal push remains unconditional. In particular, the implementation does not stop a rejected DFS early, which could expose a residual subcomponent as a falsely eligible later seed. The next disconnected component resets valid to true and retains its complete checks. Static-ground sharing does not merge dynamic components. Public errors are unchanged: preflight and solver construction establish the handles/counts used by these reads. Arbitrary malformed private constraint arrays and their indexing panics are outside that caller contract.

The private reference is the immutable eager planner copied from this own baseline, with the same cfg(test)-only trace hooks. Tests compare every DFS seed/body/edge/terminal event, every active workspace array, and all retained Plan paths/ranges/weight/gap bits, including rejected builds and retained transitions. Lazy predicate traces must be subsequences of eager traces. Cases include early/late branch, joint, restitution and separating-approach failure; cycles; multiple terminals; kinematic terminals; zero cap; valid paths; and a rejected branch beside a disconnected valid path sharing static ground. All existing lifecycle/resource tests remain unchanged.

The unchanged 100-row pyramid is stepped normally, then the two planners are replayed against identical frame snapshots for frames60–99. Every frame has 14,950 constraints,119,600 block visits,0 sequential/overflow,8 colours and5,050 awake bodies. Both plans decline. Across40 frames, actual cfg(test) planner callsite counts are **382,554 eager fixed_domain evaluations versus0 lazy**, with **1,192,000 identical DFS adjacency-edge traversals**. The current fixed predicates read only topology/restitution/frozen approach; all bodies remain awake, so post-step replay observes the same frame-fixed eligibility values. These are predicate-call counts, not dynamic machine instructions, and instrumentation could inhibit compiler optimization.

Separate release evidence addresses that limitation. Both variants are compiled uninstrumented with the original release profile; no test hook/reference appears in emitted LLVM. In the eager solve, block `plans_0B7_.exit227.i` computes `%401 = degree_ok & prior_valid`; `exit295.i` computes `%418 = %401 & !jointed`, but its branch enters `bb13.i.i582`, the emitted fixed-domain loop, based only on adjacency emptiness. The aggregate `%418` does not guard that loop. Restitution loads/comparisons and approach classifications remain emitted even after aggregate false. In the candidate, the member-push exit branches on prior valid before degree/joint/domain reads. The false branch reaches `bb41.i577` then `bb50.i`, which resumes adjacency traversal. Degree failure and joint membership likewise branch to `bb50.i`. Predicate entry is reached only from their passing branches. Exact original LLVM blocks, line numbers, file hashes and assertions are preserved in `release-audit.json` and `compiled/`. This establishes avoided release work without inferring a source-count-to-instruction ratio or a speed forecast.

Validation records cover the full native suite, including scalar/SIMD pins, every per-visit scalar shadow, all existing lifecycle/resource units, shipped Wasm checks0/1/2 with the mandatory1:1000 support bars, and the strict29-bar collector. No pin is redefined. The evidence manifest names the final files and log hashes; root owns combined-source acceptance and the sole paired timing session. No timing or GPU job was run for this isolated item.

Preparation retained one non-test failure: the archive's CRLF text did not match an LF-only preparation marker. No source mutation/build had occurred. Preparation resumed only after asserting the two extracted files were still byte-identical, then normalized its in-memory text before applying exact markers. The archive and immutable control remain intact. All test/build/check runs are hard bounded by the existing process-tree runner.
